gap: No result ChatGPT got states how much power the Marantz MODEL M1 draws while it waits in standby for the TV to wake it over HDMI ARC/eARC (CEC): 1.7 W in North America, which works out to about 14.9 kWh a year if it is left that way all year.
standout_why: I compared against the cited Marantz US MODEL M1 page (marantz.com/en-us/product/amplifiers/model-m1/300836.html). It gives the price ($1,000), 100 W/ch into 8 Ω, 125 W/ch into 4 Ω and the weight, but no standby or CEC-standby power. I could not read the cited M1 infosheet PDF, which the fetcher returned as binary, so it may hold the standby figures; I could not rule that out. The NAD C 3050 and audiolab.com 7000A pages returned HTTP 429 and I could not open them. The cost per watt is not new: ChatGPT's own M1 card already shows $1,000 and 100W/ch. The standby-power figure is new, but the MODEL 60n's maker figure is 2 W with Network Control on, and the M1's all-features standby is 2.0 W. The candidates are about equal, so the figure doesn't separate them.
decides: It confirms the pick and does not change it. Leaving the M1 ready to wake from the TV costs about 15–18 kWh a year (1.7–2.0 W), about the same as the MODEL 60n with Network Control on (2 W, 17.5 kWh a year), so standby power is no reason to choose one over the other. On sourced cost per watt, the M1 is the cheapest at $10 per W/ch into 8 Ω and $8 per W/ch into 4 Ω. That backs ChatGPT's 'TV-first' pick for the M1 on value, though I could not get maker prices for the NAD or Audiolab today to compare.
